mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions and rising corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without any threshold condition.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where PAYEMS increases by at least 50,000 jobs month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 4.5% in a consecutive monthly reading, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In months where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: The joint signal of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and declining industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a tightening monetary policy coinciding with weakening supply, which compresses corporate margins and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal from the FEDFUNDS rise and INDPRO decline fails to materialize in more than 55% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market expansion regime (HOUST > 1300 thousand units) and strong retail sales (RSAFS > 700,000 million dollars), consumer spending momentum drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: housing market expansion with strong retail sales
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months meeting the HOUST>1300 and RSAFS>700000 condition.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals expanding manufacturing activity and rising corporate output, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without any threshold condition.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% in a consecutive monthly reading, it signals an overheating labor market that may prompt aggressive central bank action, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In months where UNRATE is below 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the core consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 325.0 in a consecutive monthly reading, it signals accelerating inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In months where CPIAUCSL exceeds 325.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation and monetary tightening regime (CPIAUCSL > 325.0 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the combination of rising prices and higher interest rates compresses equity valuations, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months meeting the CPIAUCSL>325.0 and FEDFUNDS>4.5 condition.
